pages.Teach_Her_To_Land: Observe the hands, not the flourish. Crono caught Sera gently and let Marle see the damage. His wrist held its hairline; Guardia gained wards against the Debt. No miraculous new father underneath. Just the copy stamped Crono-41 learning that a catch need not become a cage.
pages.Hold_The_Copy_Together: A sleeve over the wrist, a sword through the gate. Splendid concealment; dreadful repair. Crono's shell cracked further, Vaelos found more room to whisper, and Sera's escape took the shape of ink. I know this trick. The audience watches the intact face while the hand beneath it breaks.

pages.set: One bowl, containing both the breakfast and its ash! Crono caught it with a dash that cost him porcelain. Nothing inside became innocent again. Vaelos remembered the catching, though. Of all the demonstrations my dolls have given, this is the one I wish I had put in their instructions.

Atrium_Dummy.title: The First One on the Workbench

pages.Spared: Our training marvel survived the lesson. Under those improbable shields was a failed Crono, older than the copy you brought home. You stopped before turning him into stock. I used to call a doll a failure when nobody wanted it. A useful definition for keeping the blame off the maker.
pages.Salvaged: The ring came out; an arm cannon went into the tally. The masks began their black weeping, the music box acquired a hydraulic hiss, and Glenn withheld his Dual Techs. Efficient work. I once used that word for a body assembled around a missing boy. It did not make the boy less missing.

pages.set: Sera's little fairground doll met the failed copy at the training ring. Two versions of the same face, and the canvases collided around them. An Amber Rift, ladies and gentlemen, with no concealed mirror. I had numbered my mistakes to keep them apart. The dolls did not respect the filing system.

pages.Told: Crono offered Marle his wrist. Not a revelation for the queen; she had been checking it for warmth all along. The gold-leaf repair path opened in the Bone-Tree. An excellent disappearing act in reverse: the secret remained true, and the hiding went away.
pages.Hidden: Down came the sleeve. Marle was not fooled, but the crack stayed out of sight, and my backstage rubber reseal remained a possible answer. A patch can hold without telling the truth. I know precisely how to sell one. That is not a recommendation.

pages.set: At last, the clown identified the hands behind the trick: mine. The copy, the assembly, the boy whose place it took. My confession gave a little of Crono's ceiling back. Not his original body. Not twenty-four years without fear. Keep the applause until I have learned the difference.

I kept the account behind my smile. The Mask of No One was easier to offer than an explanation; confession would have to wait for camp. Such a generous performer, furnishing everyone with faces. Such a careful coward, making certain nobody saw his own.

pages.Granted: Glenn offered Ashen Bash and Mercy Leap: room beside him, not merely lessons from a distance. His judgement had allowed those hands to work together. No ribbon for me, please. Trust belongs to the people doing the catching, not the fellow who manufactured the need.
pages.Refused: The Marshall read the record and withheld his Dual Techs. Killing the spareable had made cooperation something he would not perform. Repairing the Bekkler doll could open that door again. Notice the condition: mend something. My usual offer of a better mask would not do.

Pipe_Overload.title: A Hundred Years in the Furnace

pages.Left: The pipes were left alone. Truce's future was not burned for this charge of the Atrium. A modest exhibit: no flare, no triumphant spin of the clock hands. Merely a hundred years not spent here. I used to find restraint terribly difficult to advertise.
pages.Overclocked: The Atrium received its charge; a hundred years of Truce's future went into the pipes. Hear that fine industrious hum. It is much easier to call a thing fuel when the people who would have lived in it have not arrived to object.

pages.Saved: Robo's old heart was kept from selfish use. Its help remained a trust, with Lucca's consent part of the arrangement. I can show you a heart that works; I cannot stamp permission onto its casing. The distinction has been expensive for my customers to teach me.
pages.Burned: The Core was used without Lucca's consent. Golden repair was barred, and the Atropos Ribbon would fail when called upon. A working heart, an unanswered question: behold how readily we mistake the first for an answer to the second. I have built an entire career on that mistake.

pages.Equipped: The ribbon was fitted to the Prometheus Core, protecting the rewound R-66Y from Dark changes for one cycle. A small knot, not a pardon for everything done elsewhere. The child kept his childhood while the rest of the ledger remained legible. No vanishing ink was included.
pages.Lost: No ribbon remained to shelter a rewound R-66Y from later Dark changes. This page does not say he must become a cannon; other decisions still have their pages. It records the protection that was lost. I am trying, rather late, not to sell an absence as a certainty.

pages.Grown: Water, return, water again: hardly the pace of a respectable miracle. Doan's seed grew into a gramophone flower, remembering a future where Crono was never vaporised. It could hold the Atrium gate against the siege. The little thing accomplished this without pretending the siege would never come.
pages.Ash: Doan's seed became ash, burned for fuel or lost with the Arris Dome. Its remembered future did not grow here. I could put the ash in a handsome pot and label it a beginning. You would still be standing before the place where a flower ought to answer.

pages.Rescued: The child in R-66Y's tank was rescued rather than spent as a tachyon heart. She grew at the Atrium pool and offered passage to stabilised gates. A copy helping a copy get home. I would call it a successful model, if the word did not make children sound replaceable.
pages.Lost: The clone did not reach her place beside the Atrium pool. Without her, the walk through Truce exacted more Debt. An empty place is not a shortcut waiting to be repaired. My profession taught me to answer absence with another body. This page refuses the substitution.

pages.set: At the dummy, Sera chose the disappearance instead of merely suffering it. The training ring could not make the choice painless. It did make this an earlier promise she might carry to the Heart: leaving for a moment need not mean being abandoned. Please do not applaud over the silence.

pages.Repainted: Three mornings the house was saved, and the vein was sealed. The dojo opened; Ashen Morning lasted longer. A fresh beginning, says the barker. Look closer, says the keeper: the char has a history, and no coat of paper can make those earlier mornings unhappen.
pages.Incinerated: The town burned through its repeated mornings, and Krona kept drinking. Crimson Night stayed; the family's room survived as a flake of gold leaf. Portable remembrance! What a convenient size for the people leaving. The home itself did not fit in anybody's pocket.
pages.Both: A sealed vein and a kept vial, on the same page. Krona held the doll and the contradiction: the source stopped, the sipping not renounced. Neither half cancels the other. I have seen ledgers make a loss disappear by changing columns. This one leaves both hands in view.

pages.Sealed: The vein closed. Oil-Drinker ended, the retainers could finally rest, and Krona's corruption began to clear. Then came the less spectacular work: asking someone else to take a hit. My own preservation tricks seldom included instructions for letting go. Hers had to be learned without them.
pages.Kept: Krona kept drinking, and the gourd kept answering. It held her up while Ruin accumulated across the worlds. The retainers behind their masks were not an abstract argument to her. Here is the trouble with my finest preservation work: it makes stopping feel like abandoning someone twice.

pages.Taken: The Founder's blade left its stand and stained other skies with cobalt, showing hidden slips. At home, Crimson Night became permanent. A sunrise you can carry! I should have warned you that portability is sometimes another name for taking something from everyone who stayed.
pages.Left: The nodachi stayed blue in the vault; Krona went toward the Furnace with rust. The blade did not take the island's morning away. That is not a guarantee of dawn after every other choice. A keeper must distinguish the harm you declined from the harm the world still holds.

Ashinaga.title: The Petition He Could Not Finish

pages.Rested: Krona folded the petitions over Ashinaga and let her father figure rest. U1 kept its ink parry; his fibre did not become another weapon. No grand resurrection under the cloth. I am beginning to understand that a final kindness need not bring its recipient back for an encore.
pages.Ripped: Ashinaga's Lavos fibre was torn out for the blade. A weapon and a Ruin field entered the account; the island's masks began to weep oil without end. The man who raised Krona became something she could carry into battle. I cannot pretend that transformation is unfamiliar to me.

pages.Reforged: Atropos-00's ribbon joined the reforging, and the Masamune became part of the Cobalt Nodachi's upgrade. An old blade given another working shape. We makers adore that phrase. Remember the ribbon, though: the work was not accomplished by steel deciding it had no history.
pages.Shattered: The Masamune was broken for its chitin. Useful material, entered neatly where a blade had been. Nothing in the tally requires me to call the fragments worthless. Nothing in their usefulness requires me to pretend the blade was kept. A difficult balance for a salesman.

Krona_Joined.title: Two Ways to Survive a Fall

pages.set: The duel did not end with a corpse. Later, among the repainted streets and masked retainers, Krona joined Crono. Their two canvases could strike together. What a pair to put on a poster: one kept alive by my porcelain, one by the vein. Neither looked particularly grateful for the comparison.

The Daimyo's petitions scattered, exposing Krona's childhood name beneath the correction. Ruin Purge followed that first Break, but do not mistake the lesson for the discovery. He had kept the child's name. I kept serials. It is unpleasant to find myself envying a man made of surrender forms.

A clay gear fell out of tomorrow and into the Chitin-Pagoda. It stuttered to a different beat than the ink around it. Two worlds for the price of one ceiling! Forgive the patter. When a house begins receiving another world's machinery, a cheerful announcement is seldom useful shelter.

The vein was sealed, but Krona first kept one vial. There it is: small enough to hide in a hand, large enough to keep the contradiction alive. This was part of the way to Goyama's Both, not proof that every paradox had already been completed. I have overpromised with smaller bottles.

The Tanaka house survived three mornings. Its family tore away the covering paper, left the char visible, and made a dojo of the house. A school with the damage showing! I have sold immaculate facades for years. Nobody learned much from them except where not to look.

The Weeping Shogun fell, ink and clay no longer holding one body together. Vaelos took Sera's cage up the seam; Johnny's surviving wheel towed the party after her. End of the act, not end of the chase. Chasing a cage is not yet bringing its prisoner home.

pages.Sleeping: Cassia brought the uploaded choir to sleep without burning its people. The seed remained alive, and mercy left the Core behind Doan's gate rather than free among the ashes. Listen: quiet, not extinction. I have spent too many years presenting the difference as an optional refinement.
pages.Incinerated: The porcelain citizens burned. Orange remained in the sky; the Core lay free, while the seed and the ribbon's path were lost. The vendors returned as charcoal outlines with grief in their prices. A remarkable bargain, if you read only the line marked free. I used to print that line largest.

pages.Rewound: The great Curator's old chassis gave way to a small child-frame. He could teach Wire Loom Mend; the clone was rescued, and Cassia kept her many-legged climb. His number remained R-66Y. Numbers can identify someone without sentencing them to the job they were first built to do. I am learning.
pages.Salvaged: The Curator became a cannon, and Empress Cannon entered the party's repertoire. Cassia acquired two legs instead of her climbing frame; Lucca's voice dimmed. Azar would hear what had happened. A barrel has a simpler future than a child. That was precisely the attraction, was it not?

pages.Sleep: Mother Brain was put to sleep, not driven harder. On the child's road, her harmony could join the lullaby. No guarantee of that whole ending comes with this page. Merely the possibility of a voice returning as accompaniment instead of an order. I should have made more room for accompaniment.
pages.Overclock: Mother Brain was overclocked, burning a hundred years of the future for power. The machine answered the demand. So obliging, these devices with no empty line on which to write refusal. I assembled something very obliging once, and called its endurance a happy ending.

pages.Asked: Lucca was asked before her work was used. The amber answered with steadier mercury and the warmth of cooperation. Neither genius nor need had made the question unnecessary. For my next trick, I shall wait for an answer. It should not have taken a whole ledger to teach me how.
pages.Forced: The work was forced. Resentment gathered; the amber dimmed and Lucca's voice lost its warmth. The machinery could still obey without making the act consensual. A subtle distinction, if you stand far enough from the tank. I invite you to observe where the maker usually chooses to stand.

pages.Keep_Integrated: Cassia remained, and her voice became plural while Lucca faded into a hum. Not Lucca restored in a convenient new body; not Cassia quietly erased. Two intents continuing in one frame. I can inventory the parts. I cannot tell you that their answer ought to have been mine.
pages.Extract: Cassia shut down and left the party; Lucca's Last Schematic remained, allowing another ally to reinforce Crono. A horn gone quiet, instructions still usable. Do not let me sell you those instructions as the same companion. Nor let the quiet decide, by itself, whether permission was asked. That has its own page.

pages.Rescued: Fragments of Lucca's nervous system were brought out of the tanks, strengthening Wire Loom Mend. A rescue in pieces, with no promise of a whole woman walking out behind it. I have made that promise before. Today the exhibit will be exactly what it is, and no larger.
pages.Left: The fragments were left in the tank farm. The extra strength they could have brought to Wire Loom Mend did not come by this route. I will not invent a tidier fate for what stayed behind. An archivist's failure to bring someone out is not permission to finish their story for them.

Ferro_Drone.title: A Machine Not Counted as Scrap

pages.Spared: The Ferro-Drone was spared, and Mercury Pulse became less costly to use. There, a practical consequence; you need not pretend kindness was useless to make it kindness. The machine also remained unscrapped. Pardon me: I nearly filed that part under incidental.
pages.Scrapped: The Ferro-Drone became scrap. Such an easy word, with none of the awkward motion that preceded it. The Codex does not supply a grander justification. I have a workshop full of small useful pieces. I am trying to remember which ones I once expected to answer.

pages.Evac: The Slag-Yard was evacuated. Its traders lived to be more than silhouettes in the next account. A successful exit, with the people included! I can make a splendid door on a stage. It takes rather different work to get everyone through it before the curtain burns.
pages.Sealed: The yard was sealed, and the traders did not survive it. A secure closure, if one describes only the gate. I shall leave their absence in the foreground. Too many of my best illusions depended on persuading an audience that whoever vanished had gone somewhere pleasant.

pages.Silenced: The Oil Cathedral was silenced; the Ossuary's hydraulic hiss quieted with it. No need to announce the silence at full volume. It did not rewrite every other cruelty in the foundry. It made this particular machinery stop insisting that the world listen.
pages.Fed: The Oil Cathedral was fed, rather than silenced. An industrious word for an industrious place. Notice how little it tells us about hunger. There is always room for another mouthful in a machine built to keep going. I used to print that as a recommendation.

pages.set: The unstable amber was forced open, letting the party reach Eden before the Ossuary was finished with them. Coming back could bring spores to Mother Brain's wiring and uncover the secret beneath her graft. A return ticket printed before the departure! The nerve in the machinery was less amusing than the trick.

Cassia asked to mend Crono, and he let her. His shell healed, but its cracks kept a brighter glow: maintenance, not a replacement man. Sera could touch the result. I built the frame; Cassia remembered to speak to the person inside it before beginning work.

pages.Scholar: Azar sat and folded her wings. The library survived; Xyloph's clutch lived, and hatchlings found a little moon in Crono's open chest. Our counterfeit, promoted to astronomy! They needed neither a serial certificate nor a flawless shell before deciding he was worth looking toward.
pages.Predator: Azar's mantle burned. The clutch fossilised; the library became a war camp, and the Divinity Field became something the party could learn. Xyloph began treating them as clients. An education acquired! I hope you did not miss what happened to the school while I announced it.

Moon_Memory.title: The Wall That Took a Morning

pages.Kept: Crono kept the memory of his porcelain reveal. The Debt stayed heavier, but this choice did not close the Bone-Tree's gold-leaf repair. No prize for forgetting quickly. Some mornings hurt to carry because they are the first mornings anybody saw what you were carrying.
pages.Sacrificed: The Papyrus Wall took the memory, and the Debt eased. Gold-leaf repair was closed for this cycle and the next. The remembered sentence could grow outside Crono while its absence stayed inside him. An excellent exchange, says the counter. I suggest inspecting both sides before agreeing with it.

Eden.title: A Garden with or without Guests

pages.Panspermia: Xyloph's spores crossed into the earlier worlds: the Atrium, the ink country, the Ossuary. Eden gave up being kept entirely to itself. A garden making copies without demanding that every new patch look identical! My own catalogue would have benefited from that distinction.
pages.Pure: Eden was kept pristine rather than seeded into the other worlds. Its own garden remained the chosen boundary. Do not confuse that with a promise to shelter everything outside it. I once made an immaculate container and called the work finished. The people at its edge had other measures.

pages.Spore: The spore tether carried harm across its living net. The blow was not abolished; no handkerchief over the ledger could make that true. It was shared. I built a father who kept his damage out of sight. The fungus proposed a less solitary arrangement.
pages.Burn: Burn, rather than Spore, is written on this tether's page. Do not let my lovely lettering soften the verb. I have spent too long teaching people that what a thing held together matters less than what they can get from it. No flourish will make the two entries identical.

pages.Bloom: In this Eden, leaves grew with every Break. Xyloph's living world answered the opening of a shell with more growth. A trick my workshop never managed: something increasing without requiring a new serial plate. Please leave the applause until you can hear the leaves.
pages.Ash: Ash fills Xyloph's page where the other history puts out leaves. Do not mistake the two because I bound them under one title. The keeper's hands stay dirty whichever page he turns. Mine have learned a great deal about arranging ashes, and very little about replacing a canopy.

pages.Incubated: The egg was incubated, and a hatchling became a companion. A future admitted without first proving it useful. I could have offered you a model that arrived already obedient, already smiling. How fortunate that nobody ordered from my catalogue this time.
pages.Crushed: The egg was crushed. Whatever that shell might have sheltered would not hatch from it now. A tiny exhibit, easy to walk past on the way to larger catastrophes. I will not enlarge it for effect. It was already the whole size of one beginning.

pages.set: The frozen Moon turned red, and Vaelos spoke through Azar. The god that never fell had found a question inside its worship. Another Amber Rift entered the account. No meteor was required to make this world tremble; sometimes an impossible question supplies all the impact a page can hold.

pages.Broken: The Central Eye broke, exposing the siphon behind the beauty. Vesper joined without demanding a duel, and the cathedral could breathe. A marvellous view, once the window stopped concealing the apparatus. I feel obliged to mention that knowing how the illusion works is not what made the prisoners suffer.
pages.Polished: The Eye was polished, its perfection preserved with the cage. Vesper duelled before joining; the Weaver kept her crueler course, and the grief hum continued. Such a shining result. I have watched an audience admire a surface until the person behind it could no longer interrupt.

Moon.title: A Nightlight or a Way through

pages.Sleep: The cathedral's Moon was left asleep. Its chamber stayed intact, and the fountain became a Divinity Field. On a child's road it could be a nightlight. No obligation to become that story; merely one beautiful thing not broken to hurry the travellers onward.
pages.Shatter: The Moon's core was detonated for passage. Floating debris replaced the chamber, Ruin replaced its sheltering field, and the cathedral's enemies carried NULL. A door opened, certainly. I have listed the room that paid for it on the same page, where the price cannot fall behind the binding.

pages.set: All seven colours met while Crono's galaxy stayed open. Cracked and whole could share the image; Chrono Prism answered, and the conduit between the worlds became visible. No earlier break was secretly undone. Please watch both hands: the repair and the damage are present at the same time.

pages.Cracked: Vesper allowed his glass to crack. His pools rang with the same kind of note as Crono's porcelain, and something of the library within could be seen. A display case opening from the inside! I had always supposed the keeper ought to own the key.
pages.Preserved: Vesper's glass stayed whole. The preserved surface kept its composure; it did not offer the chosen opening of the cracked page. I know the appeal of an exhibit nobody can damage. It becomes inconvenient only when the exhibit has something of its own to say.

pages.Kept: The Tide Memory was kept, carrying Sera's remembrance of the loop into another cycle. A return with something still in her hands. My dolls were made to repeat motions. Remembering the repetition is a different gift, and not always the easier one to bear.
pages.Released: The Tide Memory was released. This page could no longer promise Sera that particular remembrance in the next cycle. Not every memory vanished with it; the Codex must keep its claims small. I am very practised at large claims. Accuracy is the newer act.

Coral_Heart.title: A Heart Returned to Its Place

pages.Replanted: The Coral Heart was replanted, and a Divinity Field grew from the return. No pocket-sized triumph to display at the booth. Something stayed where it could shelter more than the hand that found it. A heart given room: an embarrassingly simple idea for a maker of containers.
pages.Harvested: The Coral Heart was harvested instead of replanted. The thing that might have rooted there was taken from its place. Sometimes the proper label for an acquisition is simply what was removed. You may examine the empty place as closely as the prize; the management will not obstruct your view.

pages.Kept: The shard of Crono's face travelled with the party, and the Lamplighter's whispers followed it beyond the cathedral. A souvenir with excellent projection. It also belonged to the path toward re-stringing the carnival. Useful and unwelcome can occupy the same pocket; I have provided ample demonstrations.
pages.Returned: The Lamplighter's shard was returned rather than carried onward. His face no longer travelled in that particular piece of glass. I cannot promise Vaelos had no other way to whisper. Disposing of one likeness has never been the same as disposing of the person behind it.

pages.set: Crono stayed in the grief pool for forty-one seconds, listening to Marle's drowned aria. Amber and static went with him afterward. There is my number again. I will not call enduring the whole performance the same as asking for help; the museum can be built from endurance too.

pages.Cut_Down: Cyrus was lowered instead of left to hold the performance aloft. The music stopped; daylight came, and the children finally looked toward a constellation. His laurel remained pristine. A curtain call where nobody had to take another bow. I did not know how badly I wanted to see one.
pages.Left_Hanging: Cyrus stayed hanging, the fair stayed endless, and Glenn inherited the Marionettist's work. The laurel blackened; the sky remained unseen. More show for your admission! You will forgive me if I do not repeat that offer with quite the old enthusiasm. I know who has to stay after the crowd.

pages.Marshall: Pierrot-Glenn's strings were cut, and the knight could stand apart from the performance. Not the home Marshall borrowed wholesale; this Glenn still had his own years beneath the paint. A new stance, not a replacement history. I have confused those two often enough for everyone.
pages.Pierrot: The strings were kept, and Glenn remained the fused performer. The act had not become a past he could simply walk out of. See the excellent continuity of the show. Then look above him. I would prefer you not mistake a sustained performance for an unburdened man.

pages.set: Sunlight reached the calliope mirror, and the puppet threads became harp strings. Crono's galaxy and Glenn's hollow remained visible; Chrono Laugh joined the repertoire. Neither the strings nor the wounds had to disappear. For once the apparatus stayed onstage, doing something other than making a person dance.

pages.Kept: The jester's mask was kept, lending more bite to Punchline's shield work. A face can be useful without being the face underneath it. I should know. Kindly do not read this modest improvement as evidence that every joke told through the mask was freely given.
pages.Broken: The jester's mask was broken. No extra authority came from that intact face now, though the performer was not erased with it. An important safety notice for all my customers: a mask's failure is not proof that the person wearing it has failed.

pages.Saved: The crowd was saved. People came out of the danger instead of serving as its audience. A dreadful result for a show that needs everyone seated; a very good result for the seats' occupants. I am trying to write my reviews from their side of the stage.
pages.Cheered: The crowd's page records cheering, not a rescue. Hear how easily a whole room can sound delighted. I used to count every clap as evidence that everyone was well, then turn up the music whenever somebody tried to tell me otherwise. Admission to a show is not proof of safety inside it.

Tent_Fold.title: The Fold the Fire Did Not Need

pages.Spared: The tent fold was spared. Glenn's extravagant stretch could remain part of the demonstration, rather than every carnival wonder ending in a burn. Three times his reach, and still a person at the far end. Do try to notice him before requesting the demonstration again.
pages.Burned: The tent fold was burned. That is the act this little page preserves, not a warrant to declare the whole carnival gone. I used to rely on fire for a convincing finale. It closes an image very neatly. It is much less considerate about what the image contains.

pages.set: Across the loops, every stall's people were saved. Not one effortless morning with no fire; repeated journeys, different burning stalls, names brought out until none remained on the list. A complete performance, at last. Its finest feature was that the customers did not have to remain customers forever.

You stayed through the tent's full twenty-two-minute loop without ear muffs, while the laugh track took its toll. A hidden channel of Sera's opened beneath it. I had filled every pause with laughter. Someone had to endure the recording to hear whom it was covering.

Thread_Cutting_Mastery.title: Knowing Which Thread Is Not Yours

pages.set: Thread after thread was cut, and never a kin thread. Mastery, ladies and gentlemen: not the fastest shears, but the ones that know whom not to cut. I arranged a great many bodies from above. I am less qualified to teach this lesson than almost anyone standing below me.

Glenn_Threads.title: The Last Work of the Thread Keeper

pages.Cut_Mercy: The Ash-Loom Marionette was harmonised into sleep, its hold answered with mercy rather than flame. Glenn's remaining puppet memory could be cut loose. An empty costume did not have to be destroyed to stop its work. There is another lesson my backstage shelves have been waiting to hear.
pages.Incinerated: The Thread Keeper was burned, and a laurel fragment came early. An efficient answer to the ash that had learned to move empty costumes. I have entered both the burning and the acquisition. If I announce only what dropped afterward, I become the old barker again.

Glenn_Arm.title: An Arm That Admits Its Absence

pages.HoseArm_Accepted: Glenn kept the stump and wrapped it in worn cloth. The hose-arm stretched from it; no iron replacement had to pretend the missing arm was present. An origami frog had room inside the hollow. I sell convincing likenesses. This was something better than convincing.
pages.IronArm_Denial: Glenn took the iron-and-laurel arm. It brought a knight's defence and ended his stretch, elastic passage, and BP theft. Such a complete silhouette for the equipment stand. Please remember that fitting a shape perfectly can still mean refusing the person who must live inside it.

pages.set: The little Bekkler doll was mended, its hum steady again. Glenn's Dual Techs opened even after a ruthless refusal. Not a pardon stamped across the earlier pages: a repaired seam, and a way to work together after it. My name was on the doll. I wish that alone had made me responsible sooner.

Marle_Crown.title: What a Crown Is Allowed to Show

pages.Cracked_Honest: Marle kept the crown cracked, with Crono's star core placed in its hollow. He was left full of light rather than stars. The queen did not need an unmarked surface to remain a queen. My forty-one masks have managed less dignity between them than that visible break.
pages.Melted: The porcelain crown was melted for warp energy. A useful departure, paid for with the thing that had crowned Marle. The journey gained its fuel; the crown lost its shape. An elegant conversion, if you keep your eyes on the gate and never turn them toward the queen.

pages.Unplugged: Static was unplugged. Hiss left; SIGNAL was lost, and his single pure tone broke through before silence returned. The rain stopped. Do not sell the boy a lifetime of speeches because he screamed once. His freedom was not an audition for a more convenient voice.
pages.Fed: Static stayed plugged in and Hiss stayed with him. The Red Bike's power opened further, while Crono acquired a permanent deepening of the crack. A city kept running, a child kept connected. We makers like the word kept. It postpones the less flattering question of who was allowed to leave.
pages.Hiss_Lullaby: Cassia recorded a future song and played it through a past CRT. Hiss learned Sera's lullaby instead of the old devouring hum. Neither simply unplugging nor simply feeding: the connection was given another lesson. The sleeping Dome and a Core kept from selfish use made room for that improbable rehearsal.

pages.Freed: Static's throat was freed. Its pure tone could strip Vaelos's mimicry, and the boy could still be silent afterward. A disclosure without a new obligation to perform. I keep rehearsing a hundred ways to confess. He needed no speech to make the imitation audible.
pages.Plugged: Static's throat remained plugged into the connection. No released pure tone answered Vaelos from this page. Silence, on its own, did not tell us that the arrangement was welcome. That is an especially important admission from a man who once built a very quiet father.

pages.Kept: The Red Bike was kept: a light for the world-wire, a line through enemies, oil-fire leaving ash Krona could use. A ride with consequences still smoking behind it. I will advertise the range only if the scorch marks remain visible in the illustration.
pages.Stripped: The Red Bike was stripped rather than kept as a ride. Parts can travel in a pack without being the machine they came from. My workshop's bins contain quite enough inventions whose chief achievement was to make dismantling sound like progress. Mind your step among them.

Vapor_Memory_Core.title: The Evidence That Was Still Warm

pages.Kept: A portion of Crono's original atoms remained in the Vapor Memory Core. Brought to the Atrium workbench, it proved Vaelos a reincarnation, not another manufactured copy. My serial could identify the doll, not settle the whole family. At last, evidence that would not fit on my little plate.
pages.Used: The Vapor Memory Core was spent as power instead of kept as evidence. Those cached atoms could no longer be brought intact to the workbench for that proof. Vaelos did not become a different being because the exhibit was consumed. The difficulty was ours: we had burned something that could explain him.

Kami_Ori.title: Six Hands and an Unfinished Person

pages.Wounds_Kept: The party kept its weaknesses, or won them back from the Seventh Arm. Crono kept the cracks that showed his galaxy. No flawless new edition! You will have to continue caring for these people. I once believed the point of making a copy was to end that inconvenience.
pages.Blank_Slate: All six offerings were accepted. Weaknesses vanished, and strengths and shared Dual Tech bonds went with them: TRUE NULL. Such a clean specification. The bodies could still be hurt; a sheet without weaknesses was not a promise against pain. I should have put that on the cover.
pages.Paradox_Child: Three offerings accepted, three refused: neither universal erasure nor every wound untouched. The contradiction remained visible, and Vaelos could learn that Crono's atoms had made a child, not another clone. I had a shelf ready for him. Fortunately, the shelf was too simple for the answer.

pages.set: Kami-Ori made the offering: each hand could erase an ally's elemental weaknesses. Anyone accepting would lose strengths and Dual Tech kinship as well. This page records the offer, not six identical answers. A useful correction to the sort of form I used to hand people after they had already signed.

Kirie_100.title: The Last Scale in the Count

pages.set: All hundred Kirie Scales were gathered, revealing the Seventh Arm. Complete collection, incomplete reckoning: seeing the arm was not the same as defeating it. I appreciate a careful count. I am trying to stop using one as a substitute for knowing what comes next.

The Seventh Arm fell, and the weaknesses erased by the Offering were restored. Allies who had accepted and allies who had refused were needed together to face it. Behold the repaired company, vulnerable again. I know how that sounds in a sales pitch. I am leaving it in.

pages.Preserved: The fossil was preserved: a moment from another universe left held in the Bone-Tree's white. No promise that preserving its image saved the whole world it came from. I have run that exhibition. The distinction matters most to whoever is trapped inside the frame.
pages.Shattered: The fossil was shattered for a Kirie Scale. One more fragment in the count, one less held moment on the shrine. Complete your collection! I nearly said it without looking at the broken display. Old patter survives a remarkably long time in a keeper's throat.

pages.Gold: Gold leaf marked the crossing, and the sound was shakuhachi breath. In that great white, a little gold was something a foot could trust. No need for my usual flourish. A bridge is doing rather well when it makes the destination more noticeable than the performer.
pages.Bone: The crossing was bone, with a chime beneath the journey instead of the gold path's breath. The road answered each traveller in its own material. No gilt required, no velvet rope around the exhibit. My best stages seldom admitted so plainly what was holding everyone up.

Blank_Slate_Used.title: The Repair Taken out of History

pages.set: The crafted Blank Slate was used. Gold repairs vanished, the kept wounds were struck from the record, and Crono wore a pristine doll's surface again. Not healing. Not the final erasure of Sera, either. This was a deliberate step toward that white door, and the step must not be mistaken for the whole journey.

pages.Acknowledged: Vaelos was allowed to finish the doll; Crono acknowledged what he had kept and offered his galaxy. Mending became possible. This did not transfer Sera like a disputed heirloom. I can certify which hands assembled a body. I cannot issue ownership papers for a daughter.
pages.Rejected: The doll was shattered and Vaelos's claim rejected. His shields would harden in the next phase. A decisive answer, accompanied by the noise of something smaller breaking. I have found that quite often the smallest object in a room is made to bear its largest argument.
pages.Both: Vaelos held the original atoms; Crono held the years of answering his daughter. Both were real, and the doll was shown through repairing and breaking, not one history painted over the other. A family that defeats my inventory: common origin, different lives, no spare father to file away.

pages.Voluntary_40: Sera chose the Heart's phase-out. For two turns only the gold-leaf ghost remained; the silence had her permission in it. That choice could help open the Borrowed Future, with the other work still required. No keeper may turn a brave yes into a guarantee that everything afterward will be easy.
pages.Forced_40: Sera reached the same threshold and vanished for the same two turns, but the phase-out was forced. The gold-leaf ghost did not make it voluntary. I have dressed too many necessities as happy choices. This page must keep the distinction even when the picture looks identical.
pages.Avoided: Sera did not undergo that phase-out in the Heart. No ghost stood in for her on this page, and no voluntary absence could be claimed from it. Neither a cure nor a failure of courage is printed underneath. A faithful ledger need not award a moral to every unchosen door.

Time_Egg_Well.title: The Father Who Fed the Well

pages.Fed: Crono fell below the line and his galaxy drained into the Well, healing Vaelos. Whether intended or not, the transfer happened. A father feeding a son through the place where he was breaking. I know how to put warmth inside a shell; I am less proud of what my shells have been asked to pay.
pages.Closed: The Well remained unfed. Vaelos did not receive that portion of Crono's galaxy. A stopped transaction, not a refusal of all care. Even a father's gift must have somewhere to end before there is no father left to give it. The management is learning to print the limit clearly.

Crono_Porcelain.title: The Shell at the Last Question

pages.Hollow_Light: At the Heart's reckoning, Crono was hollow with light inside. Not a restored human certified by the workshop; not an absence merely because the stars were gone. The doll stamped Crono-41 had outgrown the specifications again. I am leaving that failure in the manufacturer's record.
pages.Cracked_Dark: Crono's last look carried the Dark cracks. The shell showed what its road had demanded, without promising which ending would follow. No polish for this display. I spent years making a familiar face conceal the cost of keeping it familiar.
pages.Kintsugi_Pris: Three mends to the little doll had cost Crono pieces of his own ceiling. Gold marked the work; it had not made the father unbroken. This was the kintsugi record the Borrowed Future required, not the whole ending delivered in advance. I have learned to distinguish a repair from a warranty.

pages.Gold: Gold crossed the break, marking the seam rather than denying it. A repair in plain view! What an awkward demonstration for a maker who specialised in hiding the join. I will not sell one gold stroke as the whole child's road. Care requires another hand tomorrow, not merely a beautiful finish today.
pages.Crack_Black: A black crack remained where the other page showed a gold seam. The mark could not be catalogued as the same repair in a darker colour. No further flourish is needed to make it matter. I have written enough comforting guarantees beneath work that did not hold.

pages.Spared: The Gallery Egg was spared, rather than opened with the loom. One exhibit the travellers did not require to reveal itself. A closed shell, and a hand withdrawn from it. We charge extra for the backstage tour at my tent. Perhaps the most valuable part was learning when not to offer it.
pages.Loomed: Cassia loomed the Gallery Egg open, letting its kept memory be seen. The gallery held wrist checks, consent, and the failed attempts around Crono's making. An opened exhibit, not permission to claim every secret in the Heart. My handiwork has more rooms than my confession first admitted.

pages.Cut: The navel string was cut, and Sera's heartbeat could move beyond its old measure, rising from the lullaby's pace toward her own urgency. No severed history fell conveniently out of the ledger. A bond can stop keeping time for someone without making their origin disappear.
pages.Kept: The navel string remained: doll thread and Lavos fibre still joined in the Heart's passage. Its pulse had not been cut free here. I will not call that proof of who owned the child. My trade has produced enough confusion between an attachment and a claim.

pages.set: Across at least four interludes, Sera taught the spoon: the small steadiness that keeps a bowl from becoming a mouthful of everything. Vaelos practised. These lessons did not alone make a child ending, but they gave him something to do with his hands besides possess. I should have started there.

pages.Fell: The pauldron fell away, without breaking. Underneath was skin, or porcelain painted so well that the Codex would not settle the question. Sera tested the warmth instead. I have the serial number, should you still want it. It is beginning to seem a poor answer to what she asked with her hand.
pages.Kept: Crono kept the old armour on. The pauldron remained part of the silhouette; this page offered no glimpse beneath it. Neither proof of wholeness nor a verdict on the ending. I made him a body people would recognise. Recognition was never supposed to require him to undress for every doubter.
